fields.value: [pic=4]Give us a verse! Drop some lines!

fields.title: Dialogue Text
fields.value: [pic=4]Hehe, yeah, I’m pretty curious to hear what you came up with!

fields.title: Dialogue Text
fields.value: [pic=4]PFFT! Wow ok! I had a feeling it would be something like that!

fields.title: Dialogue Text
fields.value: [pic=3]Yet it works pretty well! Certainly invokes some vivid imagery!

fields.title: Dialogue Text
fields.value: [pic=4]Heh, it actually reminds me of a poem I wrote… It has similar themes…

[pic=4]Gushing from your rear

fields.title: Dialogue Text
fields.value: [pic=3]Ok, something tells me I know exactly what inspired this one!

fields.title: Dialogue Text
fields.value: [pic=4]Heh… we should probably fill you in Rascal.

fields.title: Dialogue Text
fields.value: [pic=4]Well it was one of our earlier interactions together.

fields.title: Dialogue Text
fields.value: [pic=4]By this time, we were already pretty friendly, and fooling around here and there.

fields.title: Dialogue Text
fields.value: [pic=5]Claire reaaallly wanted to try to get my tip in…

fields.title: Dialogue Text
fields.value: [pic=3]I was wiggling around in all kinds of positions. Violet was coaxing and massaging me the whole time!

fields.title: Dialogue Text
fields.value: [pic=3]But she got it in! It was quite impressive, really.

fields.title: Dialogue Text
fields.value: [pic=4]Heh, after all that teasing… I was really on edge!

fields.title: Dialogue Text
fields.value: [pic=3]Right? We got a real silver tongue here.

fields.title: Dialogue Text
fields.value: [pic=7]Oh, I’m sure you’re really thinking about his tongue right now!

fields.title: Dialogue Text
fields.value: [pic=3]Heh… Seems that tongue can do many great things…

fields.title: Dialogue Text
fields.value: [pic=3]Anyways, that was a good poem Oliver.

fields.title: Dialogue Text
fields.value: Who knew Haiku could be sexy!

fields.title: Dialogue Text

fields.title: Dialogue Text
fields.value: [pic=4]Yeah, since the first one was more about Claire, I wanted one for Violet too..

I’m hard once again

fields.title: Dialogue Text
fields.value: [pic=3]Of course, I can just about hilt Olly these days!

fields.title: Dialogue Text
fields.value: [pic=4]Um heh… I actually had a sequel to that last haiku…

fields.title: Dialogue Text
fields.value: [pic=3]OK Rascal, you’re up! What do you got for us?

fields.title: Dialogue Text
fields.value: [pic=3]I would change it to. "How lucky are we"

fields.title: Dialogue Text
fields.value: [pic=3]It’s very good Oliver, the feeling is quite mutual!

fields.value: [pic=3]Oliver, would you like to go next? I can tell you came up with something.

fields.title: Dialogue Text
fields.value: [pic=7]I’m not gonna lie - that haiku was a lot lamer until you explained it.

fields.title: Dialogue Text
fields.value: [pic=3]Yeah, it may be a bit of a stretch, but that’s what I was thinking when writing.

fields.title: Dialogue Text
fields.value: [pic=4]We’re learning from the best after all!

fields.title: Dialogue Text
fields.value: [pic=3]Right? This idea really echos with the idea of time as a whole.

fields.title: Dialogue Text
fields.value: [pic=1]Though we see time as a day to day thing, thousands of years ago, or thousands of years from now - so many things change, yet so much remains the same.

fields.title: Dialogue Text
fields.value: [pic=4]A journey without an end - yet time marches on, and flows like a river.

fields.title: Dialogue Text
fields.value: [pic=5]It’s interesting to consider though, if "time" is the "river," then we are the "water."

fields.title: Dialogue Text
fields.value: [pic=4]And does the "water" come back in the form of "rain" and "snow"?

fields.title: Dialogue Text
fields.value: [pic=4]It’s not my greatest one. But I’ve captured a few concepts in this.

fields.title: Dialogue Text
fields.value: [pic=1]See Rascal, a difficult part of traditional haiku is the split of two ideas.

fields.title: Dialogue Text
fields.value: [pic=1]Two ideas that contrast each other, they vibrate against each other and change the context of each other.

fields.title: Dialogue Text
fields.value: [pic=4]The poem is meant to capture both, the phenomena of an instant of observing water, yet the realization that every droplet of water is new.

fields.title: Dialogue Text
fields.value: [pic=2]Each droplet that passes this place came from a glacier up above, and who knows, maybe it has made its way back here before.

fields.title: Dialogue Text
fields.value: [pic=1]Oh damn, that’s crazy. I’ve never considered the water flowing down this river is unique…

fields.title: Dialogue Text
fields.value:
[pic=4]Marching Forever
A journey without an end
The flowing River

fields.title: Dialogue Text
fields.value: [pic=4]Most haiku reflect nature, a season, and one of the senses.

fields.title: Dialogue Text
fields.value: [pic=1]But before I start. Rascal, do you remember last time when we were chilling?

fields.title: Dialogue Text
fields.value: [pic=4]This was composed during that chill session. You’ll see what I mean.

fields.title: Dialogue Text
fields.value: [pic=4]They’re most recognized by their 5-7-5 syllable structure.

fields.title: Dialogue Text
fields.value: [pic=1]But structure is only one piece of the puzzle.

fields.title: Dialogue Text
fields.value: [pic=2]A Haiku is a moment, an experience, if you will.

fields.title: Dialogue Text
fields.value: [pic=3]Today’s chill will also involve some creativity.

fields.value: Remind me what that is, exactly?
